subject: Feature insertion request: Aurum deal - per-account routing & soft-reservation lane

Subject: Feature insertion request: Aurum deal - per-account routing & soft-reservation lane

Team — looping you in on Aurum (large fintech platform). Heads-up: they verbally committed on enterprise terms last week pending exec sign-off and a short SOW. Two things surfaced in procurement that will materially speed the close if we can take them as short-term product exceptions or a narrow config delivery in the next 6 weeks: 1) Per-account routing affinity so their traffic pins to a model variant we certify for latency and compliance, and 2) a "soft reservation" lane — lightweight compute cushion that prevents heavy-tail spikes from pushing their important calls into fallback variants during peak trading hours.

Why this matters: Aurum is a 3-yr revenue motion and is replacing an incumbent. They ran a pilot that shows 2–3x P95 latency improvement with model affinity + pre-warmed sessions. Procurement wants this written into the SOW as a deliverable (not a permanent product change). They are ok with a timeboxed exception and an acceptance test (we run two simulated peak windows).

Ask: Can product/eng assess feasibility for a short-lived gated delivery that: (A) creates a per-account routing rule (config) to stick traffic to an approved model variant, and (B) reserves a small burst pool plus an automated prefetch job to seed KV caches ahead of their market open. If feasible, estimate effort (we need an engineering scope/ETA to include in the SOW). Attaching the SOW and their traffic profile.

Attachments: Auric_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW draft), aurum-traffic-profile-2027Q2.csv (hourly qps).

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Feature insertion request: Aurum deal - per-account routing & soft-reservation lane

Ben — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick clarification questions so engineering can size this: 
- For per-account routing, do they require model pinning only for specific routes (e.g., high-value endpoints) or for all inference traffic?
- For the soft reservation lane, are we talking guaranteed capacity (SLA-backed) or a best-effort buffer that is reclaimed if unused? Their procurement language matters here.
- What are the acceptance criteria for the simulated peak windows? Do they have a pass/fail metric (e.g., P95 < X ms under Y QPS)?

If we can get answers to the above, I can draft a short spec and propose implementation options (config-only vs. code path change). Priyom

Subject: Re: Feature insertion request: Aurum deal - per-account routing & soft-reservation lane

Ben/Priyom — technical readout from infra/serving: at a high level both items look implementable as a scoped delivery, with trade-offs. Notes: 
1) Per-account routing affinity: cheapest path is a routing config that binds tenant IDs to an existing model variant. That requires minor control-plane UI/API changes plus runtime read of tenant routing table. Effort: ~3–5 engineering days to wire config and rollout guardrails (can be fast-tracked if we scope to a single tenant key).

2) Soft reservation lane + predictive prefetch: options:
  - Option A (config + warm pool): create a small reserved GPUPool with autoscale floor and a prefetch job that simulates recent traffic to populate KV caches. Effort: ~8–12 engineering days to add the reservation policy and a one-off prefetcher script; operational runbook required.
  - Option B (best-effort prefetch without reservation): prefetch only, no reserved pool — cheaper but not protective during extreme bursts. Effort: ~3–4 days.

Risks: If we create an entitlement/reservation, we need a short-term billing and metering path (even a one-off internal chargeback) so we don't expose committed capacity across customers. Also, we need to be explicit about isolation: this won't be tenant-level hardware isolation, just scheduling preference.

I'll sketch a PRD and a minimal QA plan. If legal/procurement insists on language in the SOW that sounds like an SLA, we must push back or mark as "commercially-backed acceptance tests" only.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Feature insertion request: Aurum deal - per-account routing & soft-reservation lane

Thanks — answers inline and commercial urgency: 
- Routing scope: they only need model affinity for two high-value endpoints ("reconcile" and "fraud-score") which represent ~12% of their API calls but >60% of revenue-impacting operations.
- Reservation expectation: procurement wants the SOW to say "priority lane for market-open hours with acceptance windows" — they are not asking for SLA credits, just that we commit to the schedule and run the acceptance test. They are OK with a time-limited reservation (90 days) that we can convert to a standard offering later.
- Acceptance criteria: they want P95 under 200ms for the two endpoints across two simulated 30-minute peak windows matching the attached traffic profile.

If we can commit to Option A as a timeboxed delivery (90 days) with an internal billing note, we can sign this week and move to onboarding. I can volunteer to coordinate the two acceptance runs with their SREs.

Ben
